title: When Fainting in the Sultry Waste
description: When Fainting in the Sultry Waste in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 453 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Thirsting after God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When faint-ing in the sul-try waste, And parched with thirst ex-treme, The wea-ry pil-grim longs to taste The cool, re-fresh-ing stream.

lines: When fainting in the sultry waste,
The weary pilgrim longs to taste
So longs the weary, fainting mind,
O, may I thirst for thee, my God,
And still, through all this desert road,
Then shall my prayer to thee ascend,
My mourning voice thou wilt attend,

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
